entities.summary:
The Battle of Kulikovo was a pivotal event in the medieval history of Eastern Europe, taking place on September 16, 1380, near the Don River in modern-day Russia. It was a clash between the combined forces of the Grand Duchy of Moscow, led by Dmitry Donskoy, and the Golden Horde, a Mongol khanate that had dominated the region for centuries. This battle marked a turning point in the struggle for Russian independence and the beginning of the rise of Moscow as a major power.

The battle itself was a decisive victory for the Russian forces, who were led by Prince Dmitry and his brother, Pyotr. The Golden Horde was defeated, and many of its leaders were killed or captured. The victory gave the Russians control over the region and paved the way for the expansion of Moscow's influence.

The legacy of the Battle of Kulikovo can be seen in the continued rise of Moscow as a major power in Eastern Europe. The victory also marked the beginning of the end of the Golden Horde's dominance over the region. The battle's impact can be seen in the subsequent struggles between the Russian principalities and the Mongol khanates, which ultimately led to the unification of Russia under a single ruler.

The Battle of Kulikovo remains an important milestone in Russian history, marking the beginning of the country's rise to prominence in Eastern Europe. It also serves as a reminder of the ongoing struggle for independence and self-determination that has shaped the region's history.
